best_parts: node ex1 + ex1_why: the child's operation is tested as 'which step is wrong' (TR12 and TR7 distractors beside a correct step 3), then re-tested as 'why no posterior repair' (TR7 mesh-growth and fragility reasons). Same trap, two forms, clean wrong models.
node taxis (and taxis_t11, taxis_t12): tempting-then-refute feedback with a sure_note for each wrong pick; the refutation names the bowel-viability logic (K64, K63) rather than restating the rule.
node ex2_why / ex2w_t17 / lap_t17: teaches both keys (older PYQ Bassini versus current Lichtenstein) and says which one a stem wants; this is the examiner's K111 point, taught, not just recalled.
flaws: node worked: two non-interactive messages state the adult plan (no imaging, Lichtenstein, ilioinguinal warning) before any probe. Breaks ask-before-tell at the segment opening.

node lap / nerve path: O10 is missing its laparoscopic half on the main path. The lateral femoral cutaneous nerve as the laparoscopic risk appears only in ex2_t14 feedback and is never probed. TR14 is tested once. O9 bilateral or recurrent laparoscopic indication is also never probed as a correct answer (only in lap_t16 feedback).

node term (option term_t39b herniotomy): dominated. The stem says the surgeon 'darns the posterior wall', so anyone who knows herniotomy is sac excision alone rejects it at once. TR39 is tested only once in this segment.

best_parts: node p1_t2: 'ultrasound before deciding' refuted with a question the learner must answer ('What would a scan change in the next ten minutes?'). This is the cleanest tempting-then-refute move across the three variants.
node p3 / p3_t2 / r3 / r3_t1: Bassini versus Lichtenstein probed twice, the second time with an explicit 'older exam key or current practice?' question. Strong examiner drilling of K111 in two forms.
node p6: a three-weeks-after-TEP vignette in which the learner must choose the nerve from a sensory-versus-motor clue. Clinically authentic, and it re-tests TR14 in a different form from p5.
flaws: node r2 (option r2_t2 herniotomy) and r7 (option r7_t2 herniotomy): dominated. The stem's 'darns the posterior wall' or 'polypropylene mesh' already rules herniotomy out. The r2 stem also says 'with no mesh', which removes hernioplasty by wording alone. Key is findable by form.
node p6 (option p6_t2 femoral nerve): mapped to TR25 (triangle contents), but the wrong model it carries is motor versus sensory loss, not triangle membership. Trap map and feedback disagree.
nodes r1 to r7: no hint option and no sure_note on any probe. In r1 the key is the only option without a test, so both distractors share one form. Hint ladder is absent in the consolidation run.

best_parts: node emerg -> taxis_why: the reflex-reduction error is probed once as a first step and again as a mechanism ('why is forceful reduction avoided'), so TR11 is tested in two forms before the feedback is read.
node nerve (option i_t2 'one nerve covers both') and i_key: the open versus laparoscopic nerve pairing is one probe with a setting-word repair. Covers O10 on the main path.
node tri_doom -> tri_pain: the contents question and then the TAPP tack vignette test the same triangles in two forms; the vignette is clinically authentic and applies the gonadal-vessel divider.
flaws: node child_why (option d_t3, 'repaired later, at puberty'): dominated. No learner with any model of the child's defect would pick it, so it diagnoses nothing. Same problem in taxis_why (option b_t3, 'only causes pain and a haematoma').
node tri_doom (option 'Femoral nerve and lateral femoral cutaneous nerve'): a compound option is a known tell. The one single-item option is the key, so the key is findable by form.

nodes b_t1 to b_t3, d_t1 to d_t3, h_t1, h_t2, e_t17, f_t1, f_t2, k_t1, k_t2: no sure_note on feedback to a confident error, and several traps (TR12, TR14, TR17, TR39) are offered on only one probe in this segment. Re-test coverage is thin, and the segment has no hint on child_why, taxis_why, terms, lap_when or tri_doom.

merge_ideas: b's probe spine with c's ask-first opening (no worked tell) and c's emerg -> taxis_why pairing: a single segment that starts on a probe and re-tests TR11 as a reflex, then a mechanism.
a's sure_note and hint-ladder coverage on every key probe, plus b's p1_t2 scan question as the refutation for TR12.

Add to whichever variant is the base: a laparoscopic-nerve probe (from c's nerve node, so O10 is probed on both approaches), a bilateral-or-recurrent laparoscopic probe (from b's p4), and one occult-hernia probe (ultrasound first, MRI if inconclusive), which no variant currently drills as a correct answer.

Replace the dominated herniotomy distractors in b's r2 and r7 and c's child_why 'repaired later' option with plausible TR39 or TR7 wrong models (for example, 'excise the sac and add a posterior-wall repair for a child' as the tempting child trap).
